facts.text: Bridgeport was named Texas Main Street City in 2007 by the Texas Historical Commission and Texas Main Street Association.
In 2009, the Texas Legislature crowned Bridgeport the Stagecoach Capital of Texas.
The town moved one mile east in 1893 when the Rock Island Railroad opened a line, shifting its center to the current site.
During the 1920s, limestone quarries and a brick factory produced crushed stone for road construction, making Bridgeport a key supplier.
The original wooden bridge on the West Fork of the Trinity River collapsed after the Civil War began, ending the Butterfield Overland Mail stage route.
Bridgeport’s historic downtown thrives under a Main Street program that promotes preservation, revitalization, and economic vitality through volunteer collaboration.
